segments.t: Chef Barinov is woken up in Elena Pavlovna's bedroom by an early morning call from Lyova, who says he and his mother are worried because Barinov never came home. Embarrassed to tell the truth, the Chef claims he spent the night at the restaurant.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
'Have a conscience, let me sleep.' Barinov counters right away around Lyova, before Lyova can change the subject.
'Lyova, what do you want?' Barinov weighs in readily beside Lyova and lands on "nado" ("it is necessary") as the key everyday word here.
'You did not come home last night.' Reacting promptly right here, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Mom and I are worried about you.' Lyova counters calmly in this moment, steering the talk right where he wants it.
'Where are you?' Leaning in openly at once, Barinov links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
'I spent the night at the restaurant.' Pointing to the restaurant in the exchange, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Right now I just stepped out briefly to the...' Barinov proceeds evenly around Lyova, letting the remark speak for itself.
'And what are you doing over there?' Lyova chimes in candidly in front of Barinov and leans on "delayete" ("are doing", a form of "delat") to give the remark its edge.
'What business am I tending to?' Touching on the matter in this beat, Barinov keeps normal statement word order here, turning the line into a question for Lyova purely through rising pitch.
'I will be back soon.' Lyova cuts in firmly without holding back, letting the remark speak for itself.
'You are acting like a child.' Underscoring a child in this beat, Barinov lands on "rebenok" ("child") as the key everyday word here.
'Come on, Lyova is a grown man.' Touching on the boyfriend at once, Barinov links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
'You could have just told him the truth.' Barinov cuts in pointedly beside Lyova, to clear the air between them once and for all.
That wraps up this scene as waking up in Elena Pavlovna's bed, Chef Barinov answers a worried morning phone call from Lyova and lies that he slept at the restaurant. Until next time!
